## What This Is

Open a fresh clone in Obsidian and the first thing you saw was 21 items at the root of your vault. Four of them were yours.

The rest was the project's paperwork. A license, a changelog, a code owners file, a contributing guide, a security policy, a folder of release packages, a scripts directory. All of it necessary for a repository. None of it anything to do with running your life.

**This release moves the paperwork out of your way.** Nothing is deleted and nothing loses a home. The files that GitHub needs move to where GitHub also reads them. The files that must physically stay are hidden from your file explorer on the first open. And the build sequence now clears its own scaffolding when it finishes.

**A finished install shows four containers, Sovereign Command and your To-Do Dock.** That is the whole root.

## What It Adds / Changes

**One scripts directory instead of two.** `Council Chamber/scripts/` already existed and shipped alongside a root `scripts/`. They have been one directory the whole time in every way except location. The root one merged in.

**Repository furniture moved to `.github/`.** `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `EASTER_EGGS.md` and `UPDATES/`. GitHub reads all of these from `.github/` and Obsidian hides any folder beginning with a dot, so the same move satisfies both. `CHANGELOG` and `UPDATES/` moved together on purpose: the changelog points at update packages roughly thirty times and they resolve as siblings.

**`Primer.md` became `.runtime/primer.md`.** Your forward handoff is session state rather than a document you open, and it now lives with the rest of the runtime. `.gitignore` gained a negation so the starter primer still ships while everything else the runtime writes stays local.

**Obsidian configuration now ships, pre-enabled.** `.obsidian/snippets/clean-root.css` hides the four files that must stay at the root and mean nothing to you: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `LICENSE` and `llms.txt`. `.obsidian/appearance.json` turns it on. It is active the first time you open the vault, with nothing to find in settings and nothing to activate. Toggle it off any time under Settings, Appearance, CSS snippets.

**Session 9 gained a Step 9.** When the build sequence is complete it archives `Getting Started/` and `MODULES.md` into `Vault (Archive)/` and sweeps the references that travel with them. It confirms before it moves anything. Nothing is deleted, the optional paths stay reachable, and the on-ramp stops sitting in your doorway once you are inside.

**A stale version line.** `AGENTS.md` had claimed v3.2.0 since v3.2.0.

### Two defects the move surfaced

**A shell loop that would have split a path.** The CI JSON-parse step iterates a list of filenames. The new scripts path contains a space and the loop was unquoted, so it would have iterated over `Council` and then over half a filename. Found by reading, not by any test.

**A test fixture that borrowed its own setup from the code under test.** The hooks self-test writes a primer into a throwaway vault. Moving the primer into `.runtime/` broke that write, because nothing created the directory. The positive run still passed: an earlier hook happened to create `.runtime` as a side effect. Under `--negative-control`, where every hook is a do-nothing stub, nothing created it and the suite crashed before a single primer case ran.

So the suite that proves the hooks work had been depending on a hook working in order to set itself up, and the dependency was invisible for as long as the primer lived at the root, because writing a root-level file needs no directory at all. The fixture now builds `.runtime` alongside its other scaffolding.

**The negative control is the only reason anyone knows.** The positive run had nothing to say about it, which is exactly the failure shape the second instrument was added for in v3.6.0.

## How to Implement

**Nothing breaks if you skip this.** Your vault works exactly as it does today. This is a layout change, and a personalized vault that stays on the old layout stays internally consistent.

**If you do apply it, apply it whole.** Pulling individual framework files through Sovereign Sync without performing the moves will land a file at a path the rest of your vault does not reference. This release is one operation.

Hand your AI interface this:

> Apply Sovereign Ecosystem v3.10.0, the root cleanup. Show me every move before you make it, and stop if anything looks wrong.
>
> 1. Move everything in `scripts/` into `Council Chamber/scripts/`, then remove the empty `scripts/` directory.
> 2. Move `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `EASTER_EGGS.md` and the `UPDATES/` folder into `.github/`.
> 3. Move `Primer.md` to `.runtime/primer.md`.
> 4. In `.gitignore`, replace the line `.runtime/` with `.runtime/*` followed by `!.runtime/primer.md`, and repoint the two `scripts/` paths near the bottom to `Council Chamber/scripts/`.
> 5. Sweep every live file for references to the old paths and repoint them. Leave frozen history alone: `.github/CHANGELOG.md`, `.github/UPDATES/` and any dated record with `status: complete`, because those describe the layout as it was and rewriting them would make a true record false.
> 6. Pull `.obsidian/snippets/clean-root.css` and `.obsidian/appearance.json` from upstream. If you already have an `appearance.json`, add `"clean-root"` to its `enabledCssSnippets` array rather than replacing the file.
> 7. Pull the new `Getting Started/Session 9` and the updated `Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs`.

**Then prove it, rather than trusting that it worked:**

```
node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs"
node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs" --negative-control
node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/floor-gate-selftest.mjs"
node "Council Chamber/scripts/link-skills.mjs"
node "Council Chamber/scripts/check-skill-mirrors.mjs"
```

All five must pass. The negative control is the one that matters here: it is the check that caught the fixture defect, and if your paths are wrong it is the check most likely to say so.

**If you already finished the build sequence** and want the archive step without rerunning Session 9, ask your interface to archive `Getting Started/` and `MODULES.md` into `Vault (Archive)/` and sweep the references. That is all Step 9 does.

## Prerequisites

v3.9.0. If you are further back, the intermediate releases are independent of this one and can be applied in any order.

## Optional?

Yes. New installs receive this layout automatically by cloning. Existing vaults lose nothing by staying where they are.

The reason to apply it is the reason it was built: the root of your vault is the first thing you see every day, and it should be showing you your life rather than this project's filing.
